does: Whisks cold yogurt smooth and stirs in a cool, drained raw or cooked vegetable, with salt and a roasted ground spice, to make a cooling side that tempers the heat of a spiced meal.

intro.what: Raita stirs drained vegetables and roasted spice into smooth cold yogurt.
intro.why: It teaches you to control vegetable moisture so a cool, creamy side does not become watery.

how: Whisk cold yogurt in a bowl until it is smooth and creamy. Thin it with a splash of cold water only if it is very thick.
Wring the vegetable dry, or drain it well, so that it does not thin the yogurt.
Stir the vegetable into the yogurt with salt and a roasted, ground spice such as cumin.
Taste and adjust the salt. Chill the raita before it is served and stir it again just before.

cues.text: The raita is thick and creamy, with the vegetable spread evenly through it and no pool of water.
It tastes cool, lightly salted and gently tangy, with a roasted note of cumin.

mistakes.mistake: Adding a watery vegetable without drying it, so that the raita turns thin and sour.
mistakes.fix: Salt and squeeze the vegetable first.

mistakes.mistake: Heating the yogurt, so that it splits.
mistakes.fix: Keep it cold from start to end.

mistakes.mistake: Mixing it long before the meal, so that it turns watery as it sits.
mistakes.fix: Mix it shortly before serving, or squeeze the vegetable very dry.

quiz.question: What role does raita play beside a spiced meal?
choices: A hot reduced sauce cooked into the dish.
quiz.because: Cold yogurt and vegetables provide the cooling side described in this method.

quiz.question: How should you prepare watery vegetables before mixing?
choices: Add them with all their released water.
Warm them in the yogurt until the water evaporates.
quiz.because: Removing vegetable water keeps the yogurt creamy instead of thinning it.

quiz.question: Which appearance matches the intended raita?
choices: Thick and creamy without a pool of water.
Watery liquid separated around the vegetables.
Grainy yogurt that has been heated.
quiz.because: Even vegetables in thick yogurt show that excess moisture has been controlled.

quiz.question: Raita turns watery after standing for a long time. What would you change next time?
choices: Mix earlier with the vegetable liquid included.
Mix it closer to serving or squeeze the vegetables more thoroughly.
Heat the finished yogurt to reduce it.
quiz.because: Vegetables can release water as they sit; closer mixing or better draining limits that thinning.

comes_after.why: A watery vegetable has to be salted and squeezed dry first, or it thins the yogurt.
